Collagen. The overhyped supplement that doesn’t stand up to scrutiny. But did you know collagen is made by our own bodies naturally? You just need protein, vitamin C some zinc and copper. 
Our bodies are very capable of making collagen if we fuel it correctly. 

Online I see everyone obsessing over buying collagen and I get countless DMs too, while ignoring the things actively destroying it! 

Collagen has become a billion euro industry €€€
But before spending a fortune on collagen it’s worth understanding what it actually is. It’s basically natural scaffolding made of protein supporting skin and connective tissues. 
Your body already makes collagen naturally 💪

The real issue? Many everyday lifestyle factors accelerate collagen breakdown over time ☀️🚬🍷😴
Collagen is broken down by 
1) ☀️ UV light
The biggest external cause of collagen breakdown. Use your high SPF and UVA sunscreen! 

2) 🚬 Smoking
Smoking reduces blood supply and increases oxidative stress, damaging collagen and elastin.
Smokers often develop deeper wrinkles earlier for a reason.

3) 🍷 Excess alcohol
Alcohol can increase dehydration, inflammation and oxidative stress. The occasional glass of wine won’t age you but regular drinking will. 

4) 😴 Poor sleep
Collagen repair and skin recovery happen during sleep. Chronic stress and sleep deprivation increase cortisol, which can negatively affect skin repair. Perimenopause can make this even harder 

5) ⏳ Ageing
Natural collagen production declines with age, especially after menopause.
Women can lose significant collagen in the years around menopause because oestrogen helps support collagen production. A supplement won’t help here. HRT may well do. It’s also free in Ireland.

All evidence based and no hype. 

Hope this helps?

Tom the Pharmacist 🧑‍⚕️

Do collagen supplements work?
The answer is more nuanced than social media would have you believe.

✅ Some studies show modest improvements in hydration and elasticity.
⚠️ Higher-quality research suggests the benefits may be much smaller than advertised.
🧴 Sunscreen and retinoids still have far stronger evidence for protecting and stimulating collagen.
